To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain regions that support internal thought are not only the default mode network (DMN) but also a frontal-parietally distributed control network (FPCN) that helps sustain internal trains of thought in the face of competing demands from the external world.
the default mode network (DMN) and the frontal-parietal (FP) control network are involved in internally guided cognition.
the DMN and FPN are functionally coupled during internally guided thought.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain supports internally driven cognition.
understanding the neural mechanisms of conscious experience and the way in which the brain generates and sustains internally generated trains of thought that are not driven by external reality.
the neural correlates of the ability to generate and maintain internally guided thought.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DMN is a network that is active during internal cognition and that is deactivated by externally oriented cognition.

the default mode network, which has been identified as the network of brain areas that are most active when a person is not focused on the external environment, is involved in the production of internally generated thought, and that the default mode is also involved in the maintenance of an internal stream of thought, which is necessary for the generation of conscious experience.

the DMCN is not a single entity but rather a network of functionally related areas that can be divided into three main subsystems: (1) the medial temporal subsystem, (2) the medial parietal subsystem and (3) the medial prefrontal subsystem (see Figure 2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it provides a theoretical framework for understanding the neural processes involved with internally driven cognition.
the default mode network, a network that is active when we are not engaged in an external task, plays a critical role in the generation of internally guided thought.
the default mode network (DMN) is a network of brain regions that are active during internal cognition and are involved in the maintenance of an internally generated stream of consciousness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found a way to measure the brain's ability to generate and maintain internally driven trains of thought.
the DMN is not a passive bystander in internally directed cognition.
the default mode network is not the only brain region involved in internally guided thought, and it is not even necessary for internally driven cognition to take place.
